questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My boyfriend and I wanted to go on an exchange together. We also wanted to study in an English-speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Go, go, go. It is the best!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I attended the introduction days at Monash University where I was given information about everything I needed. I was also given a slideshow with information about everything. Monash abroad was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: In my case it was very easy to find housing. I had a friend who stayed en Melbourne with her boyfriend the semester before me, and she help me make contact with the same company as they stayed at. It is called UKO Melbourne, and was perfect to stay at (especially if you live together as a pair).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The contract and bond in Melbourne is very good because it is regulated by the goverment. So we got all of our bond back the day after the rental-period ended.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I dont really know. We just decided to go off campus right away. Also because we wanted to live central.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found all the courses at the webpage. This was a bit tricky, because I needed to make sure it was postgraduate and so on. But after this it was so easy. I got all the courses I wanted, and it was such a good experience to study at Monash.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Monash Abroad, my friends who have tried exchange, study help from KU.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the description and make sure you want your first priorities. In this case if you end up getting theses then it is just super easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really loved my professors! They were funny and clever. I ended up taking a courses in "International relations" by chance, which was really cool because there were several familiar faces in the classes. I think it was fun to try a different form of teaching.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had a methods course, which was quite a bit lower level, as I had a lot of methods at UCPH. But otherwise the level was high. I had a particularly interesting elective on right-wing terrorism. Overall, the level is probably a little lower than at home. I ended up getting high grades in all subjects. However, I also spent a lot of time on assignments, as I felt that this was where I really developed myself academically.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More active participation and I handed in many, but shorter assignments. I ended up handing in 12 assignments in total, which is a lot compared to UCPH. But it was really fun and more creative.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) FOREIGN POLICY OF EMERGING POWERS
2) ANALYSING GLOBAL POLITICS
3) HUMAN RIGHTS IN GLOBAL POLITICS
4) RIGHT-WING TERRORISM, EXTREMISM AND FRINGE POLITICS

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Seriously all of them!!! But espacially RIGHT-WING TERRORISM, EXTREMISM AND FRINGE POLITICS and HUMAN RIGHTS IN GLOBAL POLITICS. I really loved this course.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The study visa is super expensive. I payed 7050 DKK. You could maybe go for a working holiday visa instead.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was in generel less expensive. The AUD is low at the moment. We ended up going out a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didnt really use this. Ended up hanging with scandinavians off campus.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were diffrent clubs and in the introdays also activities. I joined the intro, but didnt go to any club. I know some people joined the surf-club - I heard good things about this.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the surf-club - especially in the spring semester.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go around in Victoria. This is a beautiful state. We did Wilsons Prom, Grampians, Great Ocean Road, Philip Island and wine tasting tours. We also went to Tasmania and this was beautiful for hiking and nature experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Too easy - as the Austalians says

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to every class. Be approachable.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The chill vibes <3 and the appriciating of the nature. At least if you go a bit out of Melbourne CBD.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try not to end up only with danes.. it is a bit difficult because there a are so many danes in Melbourne.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read all your e-mails twice ;)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the assignments I did. And in my course HUMAN RIGHTS IN GLOBAL POLITICS we did a roleplay about the genocide in Rwanda and the negotiations in UN. This was a interesting experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To do most of my assignsments alone, but in the same time I learned to enjoyed this.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
